authoringNotes: Original role-training practice, not copied exam content or a complete AWS certification syllabus.
Tier 4–5 labels require reviewer calibration; Golden/Boss remain off until curated.
Follow-up concepts are authored under distractorKnowledge and retain parent provenance.

questions.prompt: Which AWS service stores files as objects in buckets?
choices: Amazon S3
Amazon EC2
Amazon VPC
AWS IAM
questions.explanation: S3 is object storage. EC2 provides virtual servers; VPC provides networking; IAM manages access. Choose the storage model required by the workload.
hints: Decide whether the task concerns stored objects, file locations, or server capacity.

distractorKnowledge.explanation: EC2 supplies virtual machines. It is useful when a workload needs an operating system and server configuration, rather than only object storage.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

distractors: A record of account API events
distractorKnowledge.explanation: A VPC provides a virtual network for AWS resources. Its function differs from object storage, account auditing and identity authorization.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

distractorKnowledge.explanation: IAM controls who can access AWS resources and which actions they can perform. It does not provide the storage or server itself.
hints: Compare the purpose of this concept with the other functions described.

questions.prompt: Which service is suited to collecting operational metrics and creating threshold alarms?
choices: Amazon CloudWatch
AWS CloudTrail
Amazon S3
Amazon VPC
questions.explanation: CloudWatch supports operational monitoring and alarms. An audit event history answers a different question from a time-series metric.
hints: Match the reported interval with operational measurements rather than assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which service records account activity and API events for an audit investigation?
choices: AWS CloudTrail
Amazon CloudWatch
Amazon EC2
Amazon VPC
questions.explanation: CloudTrail records activity events that help investigate actions in an account. A CPU alarm alone cannot identify the identity that changed a resource.
hints: Distinguish a record of an action from a measurement of resource behavior.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of an EC2 security group?
choices: Control allowed traffic for associated instances
Schedule instance operating-system patches
Assign user permissions to all AWS services
Store application objects in named buckets
questions.explanation: A security group is a virtual firewall controlling traffic to associated resources. It does not replace identity permissions or guest maintenance.
hints: Trace the required protocol and allowed traffic path before changing a boundary.

questions.prompt: An application must identify an object within an S3 bucket. Which pair provides its basic location?
choices: Bucket name and object key
Instance type and security group
Role name and password length
Subnet range and alarm threshold
questions.explanation: Objects belong to buckets and have keys. Compute, network and identity attributes do not identify an S3 object.
hints: Decide whether the task concerns stored objects, file locations, or server capacity.

questions.prompt: Which credential approach is preferred for a workload running on EC2?
choices: Temporary credentials from an IAM role
Root access keys embedded in source code
One shared password for every deployment
Permanent keys copied into public objects
questions.explanation: AWS recommends roles and temporary credentials for supported workloads, avoiding distribution of long-lived credentials in application code.
hints: Separate the caller identity, credential lifetime, permitted actions, and resource scope.

questions.prompt: What does least privilege mean when authoring access permissions?
choices: Grant only actions needed for the assigned task
Grant administrator access to simplify support
Share root credentials between service owners
Allow every action until an audit is scheduled
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits access to the actions and resources required by the workload. Broad permissions increase exposure without solving the actual requirement.
hints: Separate the caller identity, credential lifetime, permitted actions, and resource scope.

questions.prompt: What does an Amazon Machine Image provide when launching an instance?
choices: A template with an operating system and software
A list of approved incoming network connections
A history of every account management action
A bucket name used to upload object backups
questions.explanation: An AMI provides the launch template for instance software. Network rules, audit records and object locations serve separate purposes.
hints: Identify whether the task concerns a running server, its launch template, or its configuration.

questions.prompt: A support ticket reports slow processing on an EC2 worker. Which evidence should you examine first to test whether compute capacity is saturated?
choices: Time-aligned CPU metrics and application behavior
The color of the service dashboard header
An unrelated bucket naming convention
The password age of a different account
questions.explanation: Correlate symptoms with measurements during the affected interval. A metric is evidence to investigate, not proof that every slowdown needs a larger instance.
hints: Match the reported interval with operational measurements rather than assumptions.

questions.prompt: HTTPS worked before a reviewed security-group update. The new rules omit inbound TCP 443 from the approved client range. What is the best targeted correction?
choices: Restore the approved HTTPS rule through change control
Allow all ports from every public address
Replace the application database credentials
Delete the instance and its attached volumes
questions.explanation: The observed rule change explains the missing allowed path. A targeted correction preserves the approved boundary and avoids unrelated destructive changes.
hints: Trace the required protocol and allowed traffic path before changing a boundary.

questions.prompt: A team needs to distribute static files without maintaining a server operating system. Which service most directly matches the storage requirement?
choices: Use S3 for the static objects
Use an EC2 VM as the only file repository
Use IAM as a file upload destination
Use a security group as an archive store
questions.explanation: Object storage fits the stated requirement without introducing a guest operating system solely for file storage. Access and delivery settings still require design.
hints: Decide whether the task concerns stored objects, file locations, or server capacity.

questions.prompt: Two AWS accounts contain a bucket with a similar business name. A support tool reports access denied. What should the engineer verify before changing permissions?
choices: Confirm the active identity and intended resource account
Grant administrator access in both accounts
Disable monitoring until the request succeeds
Create a public copy of the requested files
questions.explanation: Identity and target-account mismatches must be eliminated before changing authorization. Broad access or public copies would bypass the security requirement.
hints: Separate the caller identity, credential lifetime, permitted actions, and resource scope.
questions.evidence: The tool uses cached credentials; the ticket names a specific account.
constraints: Do not broaden permissions until the identity is verified

questions.prompt: A batch worker needs read access to one input prefix but must never modify its source data. Which proposed permission design fits the requirement?
choices: Limit the role to required read actions on that prefix
Allow every S3 action on every account bucket
Use the account root keys for the batch process
Permit deletes because the worker normally only reads
questions.explanation: The policy should match required operations and resource boundaries. Expected application behavior is not a substitute for restricting unnecessary permissions.
hints: Separate the caller identity, credential lifetime, permitted actions, and resource scope.
questions.evidence: The job consumes existing input objects and writes output to a different destination.

questions.prompt: A networking change preceded an outage. CPU alarms show no unusual load. Which evidence best identifies who made the configuration change?
choices: Review matching CloudTrail activity for the affected interval
Read the current CPU value as an identity record
Rotate every unrelated password immediately
Rename the instance to force a new audit record
questions.explanation: An audit event is suited to tracing a management action. Resource metrics describe behavior but do not by themselves establish who changed the configuration.
hints: Distinguish a record of an action from a measurement of resource behavior.
questions.evidence: The change timestamp and affected resource identifier are known.

questions.prompt: A rollout causes errors only for the new worker group. Older workers still read the same S3 input. Which investigation best preserves service while distinguishing credential and configuration causes?
choices: Compare identities and configuration; correlate errors with the rollout
Make the entire input bucket public to remove access checks
Terminate every older worker before gathering any evidence
Disable all logging and rerun the rollout repeatedly
questions.explanation: The healthy group provides a comparison. Read-only identity and configuration checks narrow the cause while retaining working capacity and evidence.
hints: Use the working group as a comparison and preserve evidence before intervening.
questions.evidence: Only new workers fail; the input objects and working older workers are unchanged.

questions.prompt: A requester asks support to bypass a failed approval and grant broad production access for an urgent batch run. What is the best response under the stated access procedure?
choices: Verify the need and use the authorized escalation path for scoped access
Grant permanent administrator access and document it next month
Share the root account key through the ticket attachment
Turn the private input bucket public until the deadline passes
questions.explanation: Urgency does not authorize bypassing the specified approval process. Escalation can resolve the operational need while retaining a bounded, accountable access decision.
hints: Identify who can authorize the request and which boundaries the approval must preserve.
questions.evidence: The exercise procedure requires an authorized approver for production access.
constraints: Use the documented urgent escalation process

questions.prompt: True or false: embedding account root access keys in application source code is the preferred workload credential pattern.
questions.explanation: Use supported workload roles and temporary credentials instead of exposing root credentials in application code. Root access is not appropriate for routine workloads.
hints: Separate the caller identity, credential lifetime, permitted actions, and resource scope.

questions.prompt: True or false: S3 objects are organized in buckets and identified by object keys.
questions.explanation: A bucket holds objects, and the key identifies an object within that bucket. The location is distinct from an EC2 instance identifier.
hints: Decide whether the task concerns stored objects, file locations, or server capacity.

questions.prompt: In AWS CLI v2, enter the read-only command to display the active caller identity using the configured credentials. Do not add optional flags.
questions.explanation: The STS operation returns identifying information for the credentials in use; it does not grant additional permissions.
hints: Separate the caller identity, credential lifetime, permitted actions, and resource scope.

questions.prompt: In AWS CLI v2, enter the command to list buckets available to the configured identity. Do not specify a bucket or optional flags.
questions.explanation: The high-level S3 ls command without a path lists buckets. Successful results depend on the configured identity and permitted access.
hints: Decide whether the task concerns stored objects, file locations, or server capacity.

questions.prompt: In AWS CLI v2, enter the read-only EC2 command to describe instances in the configured region. Do not add optional flags.
questions.explanation: DescribeInstances retrieves instance information rather than creating or terminating resources. The configured account and region determine the scope.
hints: Identify whether the task concerns a running server, its launch template, or its configuration.
